analysis:
Both modified files are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md. No executable code, wire, endpoint or auth change is in the supplied evidence. I found no concrete security regression.

What the docs now describe, none of it verified against source here:
- GLM-5.3-Flash admission and memory accounting. Hardware gates require M5 Max/Ultra with 256 GiB. They describe a load quotation, a process-memory ledger, and wired-residency and native-operation-owner fail-closed retention. See hardware-support.md lines 109-148 and inference.md lines 71-310. This touches TB-007 and T-029 availability, but only as documentation.
- Responses continuation retention. hardware-support.md lines 35-41 and inference.md lines 948-968 say the SDK response-object store has no matching eviction. That is an application-memory availability observation. It is not tied to a threat entry, and the supplied evidence does not show it is new or exploitable.
- inference.md line 61 says a refused SSD cache store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local /metrics only. This relates to T-041 and does not change the at-rest posture. Whether /metrics exposes anything beyond local access is unverified.
- MiMo original tool schemas are preserved on ingress. inference.md lines 1239-1264 say client-supplied reserved schema metadata is rejected.
- GLM tool-suffix validation and a fixed shutdown diagnostic that avoids logging the error payload.

The canonical threat model does not mention the unbounded SDK response store, so it may later need a DoS entry. The backing code is outside this batch, so it is a coverage limit and not a finding. The T-041 definition may want a note on the /metrics reason surface. The doc links to external platform commits, which is documentation only.
